skill.name: caveman-discover
skill.description: Find every LLM workflow in the current repository and label it, so Caveman Cloud groups spend by what the code actually does (support-reply, nightly-digest) instead of one anonymous bucket. Use when the user pastes the Caveman discovery prompt, says "discover workflows", or asks to break LLM spend down by workflow. The repo should already route through the Caveman gateway (the caveman-setup skill does that part).
skill.summary: Discover repository LLM workflows, propose durable labels, apply approved changes, and verify Caveman Cloud attribution.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: All 26 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, and inline technical identifiers in SKILL.md. The skill does direct approved code changes and repository-native command execution, creating a moderate operational risk when used on untrusted projects.

remediation.issue: Repository tests, development scripts, or curl commands can execute project-controlled behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect each command and its referenced scripts before execution, then request confirmation for network access or commands with side effects.

content.user_title: Label LLM Workflows for Caveman Cloud
content.value_statement: Unlabeled LLM traffic hides which jobs create spend. This skill discovers repository workflows, proposes durable labels, applies approved changes, and verifies attribution.
actual_capabilities: Inventories LLM workflows from handlers, scheduled jobs, workers, scripts, evaluations, and agent definitions.
Groups multiple call sites by the human-recognizable job they perform.
Proposes valid, durable workflow slugs and marks uncertain names for review.
Adds labels through Caveman SDK options, provider headers, wrapped-agent flags, environment variables, or raw HTTP headers.
Reports labeled workflows, verification evidence, unresolved names, and calls not routed through the gateway.
Keeps repeated runs idempotent when workflows are already labeled.
limitations: Requires the repository to route LLM traffic through the Caveman gateway before labels can be transmitted.
Cannot verify dashboard rows until each labeled workflow runs.
May infer unclear workflow purposes from filenames and marks those labels for review.
Requires user approval before modifying repository code.

use_cases.title: Attribute Product AI Spend
use_cases.description: Separate support, onboarding, and reporting costs by the product job that generated each request.

use_cases.title: Label Scheduled Automation
use_cases.description: Identify cron jobs, queue workers, and CI tasks that consume LLM tokens and assign stable labels.

use_cases.title: Audit Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Map graphs, agents, chains, and evaluation suites into distinct workflows before reviewing their spend.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Discover LLM workflows in this repository. Present the proposed workflow table, but do not edit files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Review Workflow Names
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the proposed workflow labels for valid syntax, clear job names, and uncertain purposes. Mark uncertain labels for review.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Approved Labels
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the approved workflow labels with minimal changes. Label callers, preserve repository style, and list calls without Caveman gateway routing.

prompt_templates.title: Verify and Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify one labeled path using the repository's existing method. Report observed results, dashboard timing, unlabeled traffic, and unresolved workflow names.

output_examples.input: Discover workflows in a service with a support endpoint and nightly summary job.
output: support-reply: answers inbound support tickets from the reply handler.
nightly-digest: creates the scheduled summary from the digest job.
Approval required before applying either label.

output_examples.input: Report results after labeling one routed workflow and finding one direct provider call.
output_examples.output: Labeled support-reply and verified its request succeeded. The direct evaluation call remains not wired because it bypasses the Caveman gateway.

output_examples.input: Handle an unclear evaluation script during discovery.
output_examples.output: Proposed eval-suite with review status because its purpose was inferred from the filename. No edit was applied pending confirmation.

best_practices: Review and approve the workflow table before any repository files change.
Name each human-recognizable job instead of its provider, model, or shared helper.
Inspect verification commands and referenced scripts before running them.
anti_patterns: Do not label a shared LLM helper when several distinct jobs call it.
Do not invent a workflow purpose when repository evidence is unclear.
Do not claim dashboard verification before the labeled workflow actually runs.

faq.question: Does this skill configure the Caveman gateway?
faq.answer: No. The repository must already route LLM requests through the Caveman gateway.

faq.question: Will it modify code without approval?
faq.answer: No. It presents a workflow table and waits for user approval before applying changes.

faq.question: Which LLM entry points can it inspect?
faq.answer: It covers handlers, scheduled jobs, workers, scripts, evaluations, agents, chains, and raw HTTP calls.

faq.question: How are workflow names chosen?
faq.answer: Names describe stable human-recognizable jobs and follow the gateway's lowercase slug rules.

faq.question: What happens when a workflow purpose is unclear?
faq.answer: The skill derives a tentative slug from the filename and marks it for review.

faq.question: When do labels appear in Caveman Cloud?
faq.answer: Each label appears after its workflow next runs and sends traffic through the gateway.
